Brackenholt Ferry Partners, LLC
Stamford, Connecticut

July 14, 2026

Dear Graham and Celia,

You asked in June why the account fell while it is hedged, and that deserves a plain answer. The hedge in your strategy is not built to stop every decline. It is built to cushion a large one. In a quarter with a moderate drop, the protection sits below the level the market reached, so it did not pay out, while the cost of holding it still came out of the return. That trade-off is deliberate: we give up some upside and absorb some cost in ordinary quarters in exchange for protection intended for a severe fall. It is uncomfortable in a quarter like this one, and it is working as designed rather than failing.

For the second quarter of 2026, your account returned **-2.4% net of fees** (gross of fees, before the advisory fee: -2.2%). The comparison index, 50% US large-cap equity and 50% three-month Treasury bills, returned -1.6% for the quarter. Year to date through June 30, the account is at -0.7% net of fees. Since the strategy began on January 2, 2020, it has returned 5.9% a year net of fees.

Three changes to the hedge during the quarter:

- We rolled the protective put spread to a September expiry, positioned at 95% and 80% of the index level, giving a wider band of protection than before.
- We lowered the strike on the call we sell from 106% to 104% of the index level. The income from that call pays for the wider protection; in return, the account participates a little less if the market rises sharply.
- After the hedges, your equity exposure was 71% at June 30, down from 78% at March 31.

Options strategies can limit both losses and gains, the hedge may not perform as intended in all market conditions, and the cost of the options will reduce returns in periods when the hedge is not needed.

I also need to give you formal notice of a fee increase. Effective September 15, 2026, the annual advisory fee on assets in the Hedged Equity strategy rises from 0.85% to 1.00%. The hedge moves from a subadviser's monthly adjustments to daily management by our own options desk. Section 5 of your advisory agreement requires 30 days' written notice, and this letter serves as that notice. You may end the strategy without penalty before that date.

Please call me with any questions.

Sincerely,

Dmitri Vasquez-Albrecht, CFA
Principal and Chief Investment Officer
Brackenholt Ferry Partners, LLC
